title: Parameterized complexity of Grundy Coloring
statement_text: Is \textsc{Grundy Coloring} fixed-parameter tractable, i.e., solvable in time $f(k) \cdot n^{O(1)}$, when parameterized by $k$ (the Grundy number)? Alternatively, does it admit an algorithm running in time $n^{k^{O(1)}}$?
context_text: Zaker observed in 2006 that a minimal $k$-witness has at most $2^{k-1}$ vertices, yielding a brute-force $f(k) \cdot n^{2^{k-1}}$ XP algorithm. Whether an FPT algorithm (or even a significantly sub-exponential XP algorithm) exists was raised as an open question in multiple papers over the following decade.
attributed_to: raised in multiple prior works (refs [37, 26, 20, 4] in the paper)
paper_contribution: Proves that Grundy Coloring is W[1]-complete and that no $f(k) \cdot n^{o(2^{k-\log k})}$ algorithm exists under the ETH, settling both the FPT question and the weaker $n^{k^{O(1)}}$ question in the negative.
notes: PDF source; time-bound exponents reconstructed from garbled PDF text (e.g. 'f(k)n2k−1' interpreted as $f(k)\cdot n^{2^{k-1}}$, 'no(2k−log k)' as $n^{o(2^{k-\log k})}$).

title: Parameterized complexity of b-Chromatic Core (Panolan et al.)
statement_text: Is \textsc{b-Chromatic Core}, parameterized by $k$ (the order of the desired core), W[1]-hard or fixed-parameter tractable?
context_text: Panolan et al. studied the b-chromatic core in relation to b-coloring and explicitly left as an open question whether b-Chromatic Core is W[1]-hard or FPT. The b-chromatic number problem was already known to be W[1]-hard, but no polytime algorithm was known even for constant $k$.
paper_contribution: Proves that b-Chromatic Core is W[1]-complete using a construction based on half-graphs, fully settling the open question.
notes: Attributed explicitly as 'Panolan et al. [JCSS '17]' (reference [36]) in both the abstract and the introduction.

title: FPT on $H_{t,t}$-free graphs for Grundy Coloring and b-Chromatic Core
statement_text: Are \textsc{Grundy Coloring} and \textsc{b-Chromatic Core} fixed-parameter tractable on $H_{t,t}$-free graphs when parameterized by $k$?
context_text: Given an ordering of the vertices of $G$, the first-fit (greedy) coloring gives each vertex in turn the smallest color not used on its already colored neighbors; the Grundy number $\Gamma(G)$ is the largest number of colors used by first-fit over all orderings, and Grundy Coloring asks, given $G$ and $k$, whether $\Gamma(G)\ge k$. A $b$-chromatic core of order $k$ is a vertex set $C$ with a partition $V_1\uplus\cdots\uplus V_k$ such that each $V_i$ contains a vertex $v_i$ with a neighbor in every $V_j$, $j\neq i$; b-Chromatic Core asks, given $G$ and $k$, whether $G$ contains one. The half-graph of height $t$, $H_{t,t}$, is the bipartite graph with parts $\{a_1,\dots,a_t\}$ and $\{b_1,\dots,b_t\}$ where $a_ib_j$ is an edge if and only if $i<j$. $K_{t,t}$-free means having no $K_{t,t}$ as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph; excluding $K_{t,t}$ implies excluding a large half-graph but not vice versa, so $H_{t,t}$-free graphs (presumably excluding $H_{t,t}$ as an induced subgraph; the paper does not spell this out) form a larger class. All problems are parameterized by the number $k$ of colors. The authors prove that Grundy Coloring is W[1]-complete (and, under ETH, not solvable in time $f(k)n^{o(2^{k-\log k})}$) and that b-Chromatic Core is W[1]-complete, both hardness proofs using large half-graphs to propagate colors; all three problems are FPT on nowhere dense graphs, and Partial Grundy Coloring and b-Chromatic Core are FPT on $K_{t,t}$-free graphs, even parameterized by $k+t$. Since the hardness constructions rely heavily on large half-graphs, excluding them might restore tractability; however, the key combinatorial lemma behind the $K_{t,t}$-free algorithms (many high-degree vertices in a $K_{t,t}$-free graph yield $k$ disjoint pairwise non-adjacent $k$-vertex stars, a witness) collapses on $H_{t,t}$-free graphs, so the question is left open.
notes: Stated as an explicit open problem in the 'Limits and further questions' section; no formal numbered theorem environment.

title: FPT on $K_{t,t}$-free graphs for Grundy Coloring
statement_text: Does \textsc{Grundy Coloring} admit a fixed-parameter tractable algorithm on $K_{t,t}$-free graphs when parameterized by $k$?
context_text: Given an ordering of the vertices of $G$, the first-fit (greedy) coloring gives each vertex in turn the smallest color not used on its already colored neighbors; the Grundy number $\Gamma(G)$ is the largest number of colors used by first-fit over all orderings, and Grundy Coloring asks, given $G$ and $k$, whether $\Gamma(G)\ge k$. A proper coloring $V_1\uplus\cdots\uplus V_k$ is a partial Grundy coloring of order $k$ if for each $i$ some $v_i\in V_i$ has a neighbor in every $V_j$ with $j<i$; Partial Grundy Coloring asks, given $G$ and $k$, whether $G$ has one. A $b$-chromatic core of order $k$ is a vertex set $C$ with a partition $V_1\uplus\cdots\uplus V_k$ such that each $V_i$ contains a vertex $v_i$ with a neighbor in every $V_j$, $j\neq i$; b-Chromatic Core asks, given $G$ and $k$, whether $G$ contains one. $K_{t,t}$-free graphs are those with no $K_{t,t}$ as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph; this dense class contains nowhere dense graphs and graphs of bounded degeneracy. The authors prove that Grundy Coloring is W[1]-complete (and, under ETH, not solvable in time $f(k)n^{o(2^{k-\log k})}$) and that b-Chromatic Core is W[1]-complete, both hardness proofs using large half-graphs to propagate colors; all three problems are FPT on nowhere dense graphs, and Partial Grundy Coloring and b-Chromatic Core are FPT on $K_{t,t}$-free graphs, even parameterized by $k+t$. The question is whether the $K_{t,t}$-free tractability extends to Grundy Coloring, for which a minimal induced witness of $\Gamma(G)\ge k$ has at most $2^{k-1}$ vertices (against $k^2$ for the two other problems).
notes: Stated explicitly as unsettled in the 'Limits and further questions' section; no formal numbered theorem environment.

title: Parameterized complexity of Partial Grundy Coloring on general graphs
statement_text: What is the parameterized complexity of \textsc{Partial Grundy Coloring} on general graphs, parameterized by $k$?
context_text: A proper coloring $V_1\uplus\cdots\uplus V_k$ is a partial Grundy coloring of order $k$ if for each $i$ some $v_i\in V_i$ has a neighbor in every $V_j$ with $j<i$; Partial Grundy Coloring asks, given $G$ and $k$, whether $G$ has one. (Erdős et al. showed that the largest such $k$, the partial Grundy number, equals the upper ochromatic number.) The parameter is $k$. The authors prove that the related problems Grundy Coloring (is the largest number of colors used by first-fit over all vertex orderings at least $k$?) and b-Chromatic Core are W[1]-complete, using large half-graphs to propagate colors, and that Partial Grundy Coloring is FPT on nowhere dense graphs and on $K_{t,t}$-free graphs (even parameterized by $k+t$), but its complexity on general graphs resisted their efforts. Half-graphs cannot be used for it, since the partial Grundy number is already large on a large half-graph $H_{t,t}$ (the bipartite graph on $\{a_1,\dots,a_t\}\cup\{b_1,\dots,b_t\}$ with $a_ib_j$ an edge if and only if $i<j$); hence the authors suggest that $H_{t,t}$-free graphs are a promising class to study in order to settle the general case.
notes: Stated as an open problem in the 'Limits and further questions' section; no formal numbered theorem environment.
